title: Jeremiah Chapter 21 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jeremiah chapter 21 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jeremiah Chapter 21 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jeremiah Chapter 21.

questions.question: Who sent Pashur and Zephaniah to Jeremiah?
questions.correctAnswer: King Zedekiah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:1 states that king Zedekiah sent Pashur and Zephaniah to Jeremiah.

questions.question: What did Zedekiah ask Jeremiah to inquire of the LORD?
options: If the LORD would deliver them from Nebuchadrezzar's war
If the LORD would give them more weapons
If the LORD would punish Babylon
If the LORD would send rain
questions.correctAnswer: If the LORD would deliver them from Nebuchadrezzar's war
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:2 shows that Zedekiah asked Jeremiah to inquire if the LORD would deal with them according to His wondrous works so Nebuchadrezzar might go up from them.

questions.question: What was Jeremiah instructed to say to King Zedekiah?
options: Thus saith the LORD God of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Thus saith the LORD God of Israel
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:3 and 4 show Jeremiah was to say 'Thus saith the LORD God of Israel' as he delivered God's message.

questions.question: What will the LORD do with the weapons that are in the hands of the people fighting against Babylon?
options: Turn them back into the city
questions.correctAnswer: Turn them back into the city
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:4 says God will turn back the weapons of war in their hands and assemble them into the midst of the city.

questions.question: How will the LORD fight against the people of Jerusalem?
options: With an outstretched hand, strong arm, anger, fury, and great wrath
With angels and fire from heaven
questions.correctAnswer: With an outstretched hand, strong arm, anger, fury, and great wrath
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:5 describes the LORD fighting against them with an outstretched hand, strong arm, anger, fury, and great wrath.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah was told that the inhabitants of the city would be spared from pestilence.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:6 states that the inhabitants, both man and beast, shall die of a great pestilence, so they are not spared.

questions.question: According to the LORD, what will happen to Zedekiah and his servants after the pestilence?
options: They will be delivered into Nebuchadrezzar's hand and smitten without mercy
They will be rescued and given peace
questions.correctAnswer: They will be delivered into Nebuchadrezzar's hand and smitten without mercy
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:7 says that after the pestilence, Zedekiah and his people will be delivered into Nebuchadrezzar's hand and smitten without pity or mercy.

questions.question: What two paths did the LORD set before the people, according to Jeremiah's message?
options: The way of life and the way of death
The way to Egypt and the way to Babylon
The way of peace and the way of war
The way of riches and the way of poverty
questions.correctAnswer: The way of life and the way of death
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:8 states the LORD set before the people the way of life and the way of death.

questions.question: True or False: Those who stay in the city will live, but those who go out to the Chaldeans will die.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:9 says that those who stay in the city will die by sword, famine, and pestilence, but those who go out to the Chaldeans will live.

questions.question: What will happen to the city according to the LORD's judgment?
options: It will be given into the hand of the king of Babylon and burnt with fire
It will be spared and prosper
It will be abandoned but not destroyed
questions.correctAnswer: It will be given into the hand of the king of Babylon and burnt with fire
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:10 states the LORD has set His face for evil and the city will be given to Babylon and burned with fire.

questions.question: What instruction was given to the house of David regarding judgment?
options: Execute judgment in the morning and deliver the spoiled from the oppressor
Build stronger walls around the city
Offer sacrifices to the LORD daily
questions.correctAnswer: Execute judgment in the morning and deliver the spoiled from the oppressor
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:12 instructs the house of David to execute judgment in the morning and deliver those spoiled from the hand of the oppressor.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD promised that His fury will be like a fire that none can quench if judgment is not executed.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:12 warns that if judgment and deliverance are not done, the LORD's fury will burn like an unquenchable fire.

questions.question: According to the LORD, who are the inhabitants that questioned who would come against them?
options: The inhabitants of the valley and rock of the plain
questions.correctAnswer: The inhabitants of the valley and rock of the plain
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:13 identifies those who ask 'Who shall come down against us?' as the inhabitants of the valley and rock of the plain.

questions.question: What punishment does the LORD declare He will bring upon the people according to their deeds?
options: Kindle a fire in the forest that will devour all things around
Send a flood to cover the land
Bring a drought that will last for years
questions.correctAnswer: Kindle a fire in the forest that will devour all things around
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:14 states that the LORD will kindle a fire in the forest that shall devour all things around as punishment for their deeds.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 21, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Inquire of the LORD about the war from Nebuchadrezzar
Deliver the spoiled from the oppressor
Warn about the fire that will devour the forest
Declare the city will be burned with fire
questions.correctAnswer: Inquire of the LORD about the war from Nebuchadrezzar
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:2 is the earliest instruction where Zedekiah sends for Jeremiah to inquire of the LORD about Nebuchadrezzar's war, which comes before later commands.

medium.title: Jeremiah Chapter 21 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jeremiah Chapter 21 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 21:6, what will happen to the inhabitants of the city?
options: They shall die of a great pestilence
They shall be protected by the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They shall die of a great pestilence
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:6 clearly states that the inhabitants of the city, both man and beast, shall die of a great pestilence. This shows God's judgment through a devastating plague.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 21:7 say will happen to Zedekiah and those left in the city after the pestilence?
options: They will be saved by the LORD
They will be delivered into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar and enemies
They will be granted peace and prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: They will be delivered into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar and enemies
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:7 explains that after the pestilence, Zedekiah, his servants, and the people left will be handed over to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon and their enemies, who will show no mercy.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 21:8 describe the choice set before the people?
options: The way of peace and the way of war
The way of life and the way of death
The way of prosperity and the way of poverty
The way of captivity and the way of freedom
questions.correctAnswer: The way of life and the way of death
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:8 states that the LORD sets before the people the way of life and the way of death, emphasizing the stark choice between obedience and judgment.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 21:9, who will live if they leave the city and go to the Chaldeans?
options: Those who stay in the city
Those who flee to the mountains
Those who go out and fall to the Chaldeans
Those who hide in secret places
questions.correctAnswer: Those who go out and fall to the Chaldeans
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:9 teaches that those who leave the city and surrender to the Chaldeans besieging it will live and have their life as a prey, contrasting with those who remain and face death.

questions.question: What reason does Jeremiah 21:10 give for the LORD setting His face against the city?
questions.correctAnswer: For evil
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:10 says the LORD has set His face against the city for evil, indicating His judgment and the city's impending destruction by fire at the hand of the Babylonian king.

questions.question: What practical lesson about obedience can Christians learn from Jeremiah 21:8-9?
options: Obedience leads to prosperity and wealth
Choosing God's way leads to life, while disobedience leads to death
Faith is unnecessary in times of crisis
One should always resist enemies aggressively
questions.correctAnswer: Choosing God's way leads to life, while disobedience leads to death
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:8-9 contrasts the way of life and death, showing that trusting and obeying God, even in difficult circumstances, leads to life—while disobedience results in death and destruction.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 21:6-7 together teach about the consequences of sin on a community?
options: Sin causes God to protect the community
Sin results in judgment through pestilence, sword, and famine
Sin is overlooked by God if prayers are offered
questions.correctAnswer: Sin results in judgment through pestilence, sword, and famine
questions.explanation: Verses 6 and 7 show that the inhabitants will face pestilence and afterward be delivered into enemy hands, indicating comprehensive judgment due to sin affecting all aspects of life.

questions.question: If a believer today is discouraged and fearful about difficult situations, what truth from Jeremiah 21:9 offers hope?
options: Remaining silent is the safest choice
Surrendering to God's will can bring life even in danger
Power comes from resisting enemies at all costs
questions.correctAnswer: Surrendering to God's will can bring life even in danger
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:9 teaches that those who submit (go out) to the besieging Chaldeans will live, illustrating that surrendering to God's guidance—even when hard—can be life-saving.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 21:10 states that the LORD will bless and protect the city from destruction.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:10 clearly states that the LORD has set His face against the city for evil, and it will be delivered to the king of Babylon to be burned with fire, not protected.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 21:7 imply about God's justice in times of national judgment?
options: God shows mercy to all without exception
God allows enemies to execute judgment without pity
God ignores the wrongdoing of kings
questions.correctAnswer: God allows enemies to execute judgment without pity
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:7 indicates that those left in the city will be handed over to Nebuchadrezzar and enemies who will show no mercy, illustrating God's justice through allowing judgment by foreign powers.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 21:6, who besides men will be smitten by the LORD's judgment?
questions.correctAnswer: Both man and beast
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:6 states that the inhabitants of the city, both man and beast, will be smitten and die of a great pestilence, indicating the comprehensiveness of God's judgment.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 21:8-9 teach about the consequences of staying versus leaving a spiritually dangerous situation?
options: Staying ensures survival; leaving causes death
Both staying and leaving result in death
Staying results in death; leaving and surrendering to God's will leads to life
Leaving causes destruction of the city
questions.correctAnswer: Staying results in death; leaving and surrendering to God's will leads to life
questions.explanation: Verses 8-9 contrast the outcomes: those who stay die by sword, famine, and pestilence, while those who leave and surrender to the besiegers live, teaching the value of obedience and trust even in hardship.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 21:7 teaches that God will ultimately show mercy to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:7 focuses on God's judgment on Judah by Nebuchadrezzar and does not mention mercy toward Nebuchadrezzar; rather, it emphasizes the severity of the punishment.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 21:10 teach about the certainty of God's judgment upon the city?
options: The city will be spared if they repent
The city will be handed to Babylon and burned with fire
The city will be protected by the LORD's angel
The city will rebuild stronger after the attack
questions.correctAnswer: The city will be handed to Babylon and burned with fire
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:10 states that the LORD has set His face against the city for evil, and it will be given into the hand of the king of Babylon, who will burn it with fire, confirming the certainty of judgment.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 21:9 offers a practical lesson about trusting God’s plan even in dire circumstances.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:9 shows that those who trust God's instruction to leave the city and submit to the besiegers will live, demonstrating the importance of faith and obedience in difficult times.

hard.title: Jeremiah Chapter 21 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jeremiah Chapter 21.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 21:12, what does the LORD command the house of David to do in the morning?
options: Execute judgment and deliver the spoiled from the oppressor
Offer sacrifices and pray for mercy
questions.correctAnswer: Execute judgment and deliver the spoiled from the oppressor
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:12 commands the house of David to 'Execute judgment in the morning, and deliver him that is spoiled out of the hand of the oppressor,' emphasizing justice and protection from oppression.

questions.question: Which metaphorical imagery does Jeremiah use in Jeremiah 21:14 to describe the LORD's punishment?
options: A fire kindled in the forest that devours all things
A flood that washes away the wicked
A whirlwind that scatters the enemies
A storm that breaks the strongholds
questions.correctAnswer: A fire kindled in the forest that devours all things
questions.explanation: Verse 21:14 uses the metaphor of a fire kindled in the forest to symbolize the LORD’s consuming punishment upon the people.

questions.question: Jeremiah 21:13 references the inhabitants as 'inhabitant of the valley, and rock of the plain.' What does this imagery emphasize in the historical context?
options: Their false sense of security and confidence against enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Their false sense of security and confidence against enemies
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:13 highlights their question 'Who shall come down against us?' illustrating their misplaced confidence in natural defenses, which historically was shattered by Babylon's siege.

questions.question: What is the ultimate fate of Zedekiah and his people according to Jeremiah 21:7?
options: They will be delivered into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar and suffer by the sword without mercy
They will triumph over Babylon and reclaim their city
They will be spared by the LORD due to their repentance
They will be taken captive but eventually return in peace
questions.correctAnswer: They will be delivered into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar and suffer by the sword without mercy
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:7 clearly states that Zedekiah and the survivors will be handed over to Nebuchadrezzar and destroyed without pity.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 21:9, what choice is given to the inhabitants of the city regarding their survival?
options: Those who stay will die by sword, famine, and pestilence; those who surrender to the Chaldeans will live
Those who fight will be victorious; those who flee will perish
Those who pray will be saved; those who doubt will be destroyed
Those who seek alliances will survive; those who isolate will perish
questions.correctAnswer: Those who stay will die by sword, famine, and pestilence; those who surrender to the Chaldeans will live
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:9 provides a stark choice between death for those who remain and life for those who surrender to the besieging Chaldeans.

questions.question: Which other biblical passage echoes the theme of 'executing judgment and delivering the oppressed' as seen in Jeremiah 21:12?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 1:17
questions.explanation: Isaiah 1:17 similarly calls for learning to do well, seeking justice, and delivering the oppressed, echoing Jeremiah 21:12’s call for justice.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 21:11, who is the intended audience when Jeremiah is told to 'Hear ye the word of the LORD'?
options: The house of the king of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: The house of the king of Judah
questions.explanation: Verse 21:11 explicitly identifies the audience as the house of the king of Judah, signaling a direct address to the royal family.

questions.question: What literary device is most evident in Jeremiah 21:8-9 where the LORD sets before the people 'the way of life, and the way of death'?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: The structure in verses 8-9 presents parallelism by contrasting two paths—life and death—highlighting the consequences of the people's choices.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'fury' in Jeremiah 21:12 (Hebrew: 'aph') primarily conveys what nuance?
questions.correctAnswer: Anger burning like fire
questions.explanation: The Hebrew 'aph' denotes intense anger or wrath, often likened to fire, as reflected in Jeremiah 21:12 describing the LORD's unquenchable fury.

questions.question: True or False: According to Jeremiah 21:10, the LORD's intention is to bring good to the city by delivering it from Babylon.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:10 states the LORD has set His face against the city for evil, not good, and that it will be delivered into the king of Babylon's hand to be burned.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 21:4 declares that the LORD will turn back the weapons of war held by the people fighting against Babylon.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 21:4, the LORD says He will turn back the weapons of war from the people’s hands, assembling them into the city, signaling divine intervention.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the theme of choosing between 'the way of life, and the way of death' as presented in Jeremiah 21:8?
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 7:13-14
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:13-14 discusses the narrow and broad ways leading to life and destruction, paralleling Jeremiah 21:8’s choice between life and death.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 21:14 foreshadow the destruction described in later biblical prophecy concerning Jerusalem?
options: By depicting a consuming fire that devours everything around it
questions.correctAnswer: By depicting a consuming fire that devours everything around it
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 21:14’s imagery of fire consuming the forest foreshadows Jerusalem’s destruction by fire as prophesied elsewhere, including Ezekiel 22:21.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'rock of the plain' in Jeremiah 21:13 when addressing the inhabitants of the valley?
options: It symbolizes their perceived stronghold and protection
It refers to the temple mount
It indicates their alliance with Edom
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes their perceived stronghold and protection
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 21:13, 'rock of the plain' metaphorically refers to their confidence in natural defenses, which the LORD challenges by declaring His judgment.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage shares a similar tone of unquenchable divine wrath as expressed in Jeremiah 21:12?
questions.correctAnswer: Nahum 1:6
questions.explanation: Nahum 1:6 speaks of the LORD’s wrath like fire, unquenchable and consuming, paralleling the fury described in Jeremiah 21:12.

theological.title: Jeremiah Chapter 21 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jeremiah Chapter 21 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does the LORD promise to do with the weapons of war in Jeremiah 21:4?
options: Turn them back against the king of Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: Turn them back against the king of Babylon
questions.explanation: The LORD states that He will turn back the weapons of war against the king of Babylon and the Chaldeans, indicating His direct intervention in the battle (Jeremiah 21:4).

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 21:5, how will the LORD fight against the city?
options: With an outstretched hand and strong arm
With the help of the Chaldeans
questions.correctAnswer: With an outstretched hand and strong arm
questions.explanation: The LORD declares that He will fight against the city with an outstretched hand and a strong arm, emphasizing His power and anger (Jeremiah 21:5).

questions.question: What fate does Jeremiah prophesy for the inhabitants of the city in Jeremiah 21:6?
options: They shall be saved from destruction
They shall die of a great pestilence
They shall be taken captive with mercy
questions.correctAnswer: They shall die of a great pestilence
questions.explanation: Jeremiah forewarns that the inhabitants of the city will die due to a great pestilence, indicating severe judgment (Jeremiah 21:6).

questions.question: In Jeremiah 21:7, who does the LORD say will be delivered into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar?
questions.correctAnswer: Zedekiah and his servants
questions.explanation: The LORD reveals that Zedekiah, his servants, and the people left in the city will be delivered into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar, signifying their impending doom (Jeremiah 21:7).

questions.question: What choice does the LORD present to the people in Jeremiah 21:8?
options: A way of peace and prosperity
A way of life and a way of death
A way of escape and imprisonment
A way of judgment and mercy
questions.correctAnswer: A way of life and a way of death
questions.explanation: The LORD sets before the people the choice between the way of life and the way of death, emphasizing the consequences of their actions (Jeremiah 21:8).

questions.question: What will happen to those who abide in the city according to Jeremiah 21:9?
options: They shall die by the sword, famine, and pestilence
They shall be rewarded with riches
questions.correctAnswer: They shall die by the sword, famine, and pestilence
questions.explanation: Jeremiah warns that those who remain in the city will face death by the sword, famine, and pestilence, highlighting the severe judgment coming upon them (Jeremiah 21:9).

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 21:10, what has the LORD set His face against?
questions.correctAnswer: The city for evil
questions.explanation: The LORD states that He has set His face against the city for evil, indicating His judgment against it (Jeremiah 21:10).

questions.question: What specific command is given to the house of David in Jeremiah 21:12?
options: To execute judgment in the morning
To offer sacrifices to the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: To execute judgment in the morning
questions.explanation: The house of David is commanded to execute judgment in the morning and rescue those who are oppressed, emphasizing the need for justice (Jeremiah 21:12).

questions.question: In Jeremiah 21:13, how does the LORD describe the inhabitants of the valley?
questions.correctAnswer: As rebellious and prideful
questions.explanation: The LORD addresses the inhabitants of the valley and the rock of the plain as those who arrogantly question who can come against them, revealing their pride (Jeremiah 21:13).

questions.question: What does the LORD promise to do in Jeremiah 21:14 in response to the fruit of their doings?
questions.correctAnswer: To punish them
questions.explanation: The LORD declares that He will punish them according to the fruit of their doings, stressing divine justice (Jeremiah 21:14).

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 21:3 reveal about the nature of Jeremiah's role?
options: He is a messenger of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: He is a messenger of the LORD
questions.explanation: Jeremiah is instructed to relay the LORD's message to Zedekiah, demonstrating his role as a prophet and messenger of God (Jeremiah 21:3).

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted in Jeremiah 21:5 when He declares His intention to fight against the city?
questions.correctAnswer: His wrath
questions.explanation: The LORD's declaration to fight against the city with anger and fury highlights His attribute of wrath against sin (Jeremiah 21:5).

questions.question: Jeremiah 21:8 indicates a duality of choices. What does this say about human free will?
options: Humans can choose between life and death
All choices lead to the same outcome
questions.correctAnswer: Humans can choose between life and death
questions.explanation: The LORD presents the people with the choice between life and death, indicating the significance of human free will in responding to God's commands (Jeremiah 21:8).

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 21:7 reveal about God's control over kingdoms and authority?
options: He is unaware of earthly kingdoms
He gives kingdoms to whomever He chooses
He has no power over kings
questions.correctAnswer: He gives kingdoms to whomever He chooses
questions.explanation: The verse reveals that God delivers Zedekiah and his people into the hands of Nebuchadrezzar, indicating His sovereign control over kingdoms and authority (Jeremiah 21:7).

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 6 and 10 convey about judgment?
options: Judgment is only for the enemies of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Judgment is certain and immediate
questions.explanation: Verses 6 and 10 together emphasize that the impending judgment is certain and will come swiftly upon the city as a consequence of their actions (Jeremiah 21:6, 10).
